items.title: Pay supplements could limit January's minimum wage rise
items.body: A published Royal Decree sets the SMI (minimum wage) at €1,286 gross in 14 payments from January 1, 2027, up 5.3%. CCOO estimates 1.96 million beneficiaries, against the government's 2.7 million. Employers can still count pay supplements towards the minimum, limiting some workers' gains.

items.title: Election rivals clash over housing, taxes, and wages
items.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Partido Popular leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo held their only head-to-head debate on November 19 before the November 29 election. Sánchez admitted he had not solved the housing problem. Both backed more homebuilding, but disagreed over market regulation.

items.title: Retirement age reaches 67 in January 2027
items.body: Under the existing pension reform calendar, the ordinary retirement age rises to 67 on January 1, 2027. Retirement at 65 remains possible with at least 38 years and six months of contributions, up from 38 years and three months in 2026. This completes the transition that began in 2013.

items.title: Richest taxpayers receive most landlord tax relief
items.body: The richest 10% of taxpayers received 73% of landlord IRPF (personal income tax) relief in 2023, a University of Alcalá study finds. The relief cost the Tax Agency an estimated €1.133 billion. Higher earners receive more rental income, and progressive tax rates make each euro of relief worth more to them.

items.title: EU advances case over Spain's crypto tax rules
items.body: The European Commission has sent Spain a reasoned opinion over incomplete adoption of crypto tax transparency rules. Spain has two months to act before possible referral to the EU Court of Justice. A separate, first-stage case covers missing crypto-market rules, also with two months to respond.

items.title: Over 1.5 million taxpayers still await refunds
items.body: TaxDown estimates more than 1.5 million taxpayers still await their 2025 income tax refund, often because returns are under review. For on-time filings, the payment deadline is the end of December; late refunds attract 4,0625% annual interest. Check progress in the Tax Agency's Renta 2025 service.

items.title: Madrid receives Voyager signal beyond one light-day
items.body: NASA's station in Robledo de Chavela near Madrid received Voyager 1's first signal after it passed one light-day from Earth. Its 70-metre antenna received the transmission on November 19. Madrid was the only station able to receive it at that moment because the probe was below the horizon at the other sites.

items.title: Madrid Assembly approves contested land-use law
items.body: Madrid's Assembly approved the LIDER land-use law on November 19 with PP and Vox votes. It aims to speed planning approvals and ease land-use changes to build housing. Opposition parties and residents' groups say it weakens public oversight and favours speculation.

items.title: Spain's Hernández de Cos contends for ECB presidency
items.body: Bank for International Settlements president Pablo Hernández de Cos is a contender to lead the European Central Bank. His rival is Dutch central bank governor Klaas Knot. Germany's plan to nominate a chief economist candidate could help his bid. Governments aim for a deal on November 26.

items.title: Tenant unions call November 21–22 protests in six cities
items.body: Tenant unions have called housing protests for November 21–22 in Zaragoza, Madrid, Barcelona, Alicante, Valencia, and Castellón. They join coordinated European demonstrations under the slogan "People over profit". The marches follow Spain's November 11 housing strike and come before the November 29 election.

items.title: Train drivers cancel November 23 strike
items.body: Train drivers' union Semaf has cancelled its November 23 strike after a rail safety deal, including an adverse-weather protocol. CCOO, UGT, and SCF had separately suspended their November 19 Adif strike over staffing and working-time rules. CSIF rejected that deal and maintains its Adif protests.

items.title: Madrid toughens minimum services in teachers' strike from November 20
items.body: Madrid's stricter minimum services for the indefinite teachers' strike take effect on November 20. Teachers of university entrance exam subjects in the final Bachillerato year must cover 50% of their hours as minimum services until January 31, 2027. CCOO says it will challenge the change in court.

items.title: Mounjaro users advised to add contraceptive protection
items.body: Spain's medicines agency advises oral contraceptive users taking Mounjaro to add a barrier method for four weeks after starting treatment and after each dose increase, or switch to non-oral contraception. A European review found limited evidence, leaving uncertainty about a possible interaction.

items.title: EU challenges Spain's foreign pension fund taxation
items.body: The European Commission has opened a first-stage infringement case over Spain's taxation of foreign pension funds and life insurers. It says equivalent Spanish entities receive exemptions and deductions denied to EU and EEA providers. Spain has two months to respond. Similar cases were opened against seven other countries.
